title: Eastern Plaguelands
body: Before the plague these hills and forests were the Eastweald, the eastern heart of Lordaeron, governed from Stratholme, the second city of the kingdom. Here Prince Arthas put Stratholme to the sword rather than let its plagued people rise, and here the Scourge made its deepest home. Blight has swallowed the land. Rot runs through the woods, plaguehounds and plaguebats hunt the hills, and towns such as Darrowshire, Corin's Crossing and Northdale belong to the dead. Baron Rivendare rules Stratholme for Kel'Thuzad. The living hold on where they can. The Argent Dawn keeps Light's Hope Chapel, the Scarlet Crusade rules Tyr's Hand, Mossflayer trolls cling to Zul'Mashar and high elf rangers guard a lodge near the road to Quel'Thalas. An old hermit keeps a hut by the Thondroril, and the Forsaken champion Nathanos Blightcaller hunts from the Marris Stead.

title: The Thondroril River
body: The Thondroril runs south along the western edge of the Eastern Plaguelands, the border with the western lands. On its bank stands a small hut where an old hermit lives with his horse, Mirador. He asks little of visitors beyond help keeping the plaguehounds and plaguebats at bay, and he is laying in carrion worm meat for the winter, since the grubs are the only beasts in the region the plague has left untouched. He asks every guest to honor one credo: race does not dictate honor. Crypt fiends of the Scourge prowl the hills not far from his door.

title: The Marris Stead
body: The Marris Stead in the southwest was the family farm of Nathanos Marris, a ranger lord of Lordaeron. The Scourge swept over it in the war, and he has come home to it in undeath as Nathanos Blightcaller, champion of the Banshee Queen. He keeps his blighthounds here and receives the recruits she sends to train under him, few of whom he thinks worth the trouble; he claims to have sent every one of them back to her in pieces. Skulls and mangled human remains lie about the fields.

On this very stead he stood his ground in defense of Lordaeron until a great wave of Scourge overwhelmed him, and he woke as one of them, his mind bound to the Lich King's, until the Banshee Queen came for him and set him free. The thing that cut him down he hunted for months, until it fled into Stratholme.

title: The Undercroft
body: The Undercroft is an old crypt in the far southwest of the Eastern Plaguelands, its graves long left to the dead. It now shelters dead troll thieves, unliving Mossflayers and zombies under Zaeldarr the Outcast, who raid the corpse pit at Light's Hope Chapel by night and carry the bodies back here to their hideout. A torn scroll by the crypt tells of a doomed troll named Hameya and a chest buried in the dirt behind it.

title: Darrowshire
body: Darrowshire, named for Darrowmere Lake to its west, was a village of humble, hardworking folk in the southern foothills, until the Scourge came. Its militia under Captain Joseph Redpath, a company of troops and paladins of the Silver Hand stood against the ghoul lord Horgus and the death knight Marduk the Black, and the village did not survive the night. Now it is silent ruin. In one house the ghost of a little girl, Pamela Redpath, still waits for her father to come home, and pieces of her lost doll lie scattered through the town.

title: Corin's Crossing
body: Corin's Crossing grew up where the roads met between Andorhal, Darrowshire, Stratholme and Tyr's Hand. The Scourge holds it now. Dark casters and summoners of the Cult of the Damned work among ghouls, shriekers and stitched horrors, and unseen servants walk its streets. Many of its ghouls were once the good folk of Darrowshire, still bound in their rotting bodies. Old battles cling to the place: near here a dwarf captain shattered the sword of Marduk the Black on his shield.

title: The Infectis and Pestilent Scars
body: Two great wounds cut the land west and south of Corin's Crossing. The Infectis Scar was made by dark magic. When the rune-laden sword of Marduk the Black broke against a dwarf's shield, the blade sank into the earth and corrupted it, eating out the gorge that bears its sickness still; the shattered sword lies at its bottom, and spectral marauders and corpses stalk its floor. The Pestilent Scar is a natural rift, but the plague has found it all the same. Living decay and rotting sludges ooze along both gorges, and the bones of the land show through the rock.

title: Blackwood Lake
body: Blackwood Lake lies northwest of Corin's Crossing, its waters fouled and stalked by plague monstrosities. A town named Blackwood once stood here, burned by orcs in the Second War and remembered as the home of Grand Marshal Othmar Garithos. Its waters hold a darker relic. After the Battle of Darrowshire the Scourge carried off the skull of the fallen ghoul lord Horgus to spread dread, and when paladins of the Silver Hand destroyed the company that bore it, they cast the skull into the lake. Spectral betrayers and defenders still fight along its shores, as if that night has never ended.

title: Tyr's Hand
body: In the southeast stands Tyr's Hand, a walled city named for an ancient keeper and one of the oldest holy sites of the Church of the Light. The Scarlet Crusade rules it now as its stronghold in the east. Warders, praetorians, clerics and archmages fill its streets, inquisitors keep their own grim watch, and the Scarlet Basilica rises at its heart. Crusader Lord Valdelmar commands within, with High General Abbendis close at hand, and each day a courier rides in with reports from the Crusade's command in Stratholme. A camp outside the walls marks how far the Crusade dares to reach.

title: Light's Hope Chapel
body: Light's Hope Chapel was among the oldest and most revered holy sites of the Eastweald, and the remains of Lordaeron's heroes lie in the catacombs beneath it. The Argent Dawn has made it the headquarters of its war on the Scourge, under Lord Maxwell Tyrosus. Horde and Alliance alike are welcome. The Dawn's officers hand out its commission and pay for the scourgestones brought back from the field, a demolitions man takes contracts against Scourge buildings, and a caretaker tosses the corpses carried in from the field into a pit below.

Shadowmages and dark adepts of the cult keep company with stitched golems, dread weavers and hulking Scourge champions, some of them veterans of the slaughter at Darrowshire, while banshee death singers and unseen eyeless watchers drift among them. A cult deathspeaker named Selendre is sometimes seen in the glade.

title: Northdale
body: Northdale was a hamlet in the northeast of the Eastweald until the war tore through it, and only the dead keep it now. Banshee death singers wail among the ruins, unseen eyeless watchers keep their vigil in the streets, and blighted horrors and monstrous plaguebats roam the ground around it. West of the town crawls Borelgore, a bloated maggot beast whose girth grows with everything it eats, and which has cost the Blightcaller whole regiments.

Here he threw down its standard and renounced all he had known, and the tattered banner still lies where it fell.

body: Zul'Mashar in the far northeast is the capital of the Mossflayers, a small tribe of forest trolls worn down by long wars with the humans of Lordaeron. The plague has found them too. Shadowhunters, scouts and cannibals crowd the ruins under Warlord Thresh'jin, and above them rises the ziggurat of Mazra'Alor. Scholars seek the Mosh'aru tablets held here, said to speak of Hakkar.

title: Quel'Lithien Lodge
body: In the northern hills, near the road that leads on to Quel'Thalas, stands Quel'Lithien Lodge, a hunting lodge of the high elves that once hosted Farstrider rangers. Rangers, pathstriders and woodsmen keep it still under Ranger Lord Hawkspear, friendly to the Alliance and quick to draw on the Horde. Nearby lives the priestess Aurora Skycaller, who grieves that her people are as shattered as any broken relic, yet will mend an old highborne crystal for those who ask sincerely.

body: Four old towers of Lordaeron stand over the Eastern Plaguelands: Crown Guard Tower in the south, Eastwall Tower in the east, the Northpass Tower near the road to the north, and Plaguewood Tower at the edge of the blighted forest. All were left empty when the kingdom fell, abandoned since the days of Lordaeron, and plaguebats, plaguehounds and carrion devourers now prowl around their walls. Banners still hang from their poles, waiting for someone to claim them.

title: Plaguewood
body: The Plaguewood spreads south of Stratholme, the most diseased corner of a diseased land. It was once a fair woodland that Prince Arthas crossed on his road to the city; since the Culling the blight has swollen it with giant mushrooms and rot. The Scourge has raised ziggurats and slaughterhouses among the trees, guarded by stitched horrors, cannibal ghouls and cursed mages, and the Argent Dawn pays demolition crews to bring them down.

body: Terrordale was a small town at the western edge of the Plaguewood, now a ghost town of plagued swine and Scourge soldiers. It still has a merchant. Augustus the Touched was lodging at the inn when the Scourge came, and he has been here ever since, eager to buy and sell anything at prices he calls insane, if only someone would fetch the receipt book he left in his room. Sharing his house is Egan, a dwarf who hates the Scourge but pities its victims, and who has built a blaster to free the restless souls of Stratholme.

title: Stratholme
body: Stratholme was the second city of Lordaeron and the seat of the Eastweald. When the plague reached it in tainted grain, Prince Arthas ordered its people put to death before they could rise, and the city burned. Many chose the flames over becoming Scourge, and their restless spirits still walk its streets. Today Baron Rivendare holds most of the city for Kel'Thuzad, while the Scarlet Crusade has walled itself into the Scarlet Bastion under its Grand Crusader. On its eastern side, at Eastwall Gate, a service entrance leads into the Elders' Square.

title: Tirion Fordring
body: For years Tirion Fordring has lived as a hermit in a small hut by the Thondroril, with his old horse Mirador for company. He holds to one credo and asks every guest to respect it: race does not dictate honor. He has known orcs as honorable as the noblest knights and humans as vile as the most ruthless Scourge, though he will not bore a visitor with tales of his youth. The Plaguelands are hard on an old man, and he gladly accepts help keeping the beasts at bay and filling his larder for the winter.

body: In life Nathanos Marris was a ranger lord of Lordaeron, trained by the high elves to a rank no other human had held. Now, as Nathanos Blightcaller, he is among the first and most dedicated champions of the Banshee Queen. He keeps the Marris Stead with his blighthounds, roaming the wastes to slay all Scourge and Alliance that cross his path, and trains the recruits the Dark Lady sends him with open contempt, calling every one of them imbecile. He guards the secrets of his mortal life jealously. To the Alliance he is a hero lost.

He keeps to the church and grants audience to outsiders only rarely; years can pass between such honors, and the Argent Hold, the Dawn's sealed vault, stays locked until a champion has truly earned it.

He holds that anything taken to an extreme endangers the world, the Scarlet Crusade's blind zealotry above all, and he counsels his champions to be tolerant yet rigid in their beliefs. He takes a keen interest in the Crusade's archivist in Stratholme and the records he guards.

body: Captain Joseph Redpath led Darrowshire's militia when the Scourge attacked, and he fought bravely until the death knight Marduk the Black rode up to him in the thick of battle and tore his spirit loose with black magic. Twisted into an evil shadow of himself, he spread his taint among the defenders, who turned on their allies and slaughtered the town. His cracked shield was cast aside, his corrupted spirit went on to ravage Lordaeron, and his daughter Pamela was left waiting for him. Only by changing the course of that battle can his soul be won back.

title: The Fordring Redemption
body: The hermit by the Thondroril asks small things first. He would have the plaguehounds and their runts thinned, the plaguebats cleared from the skies and several hundred pounds of carrion worm meat laid in for the winter, since the grubs are the only beasts the plague has spared. He warns of the Scarlet Crusade, which kills any who do not bear its mark, and of wild beasts the blight has made into man eaters. He offers little in return but a warm meal and talk of days long past, yet he watches each helper closely, for few would selflessly aid an old and forgotten hermit.

From Northdale came the Silver Hand standard he threw down there in despair, as glorious to Tirion in its tattered state as the day he first swore his oath.

parts.body: Last came the painting. On Caer Darrow the ghost of the artist Renfray remembered the portrait he had painted of the Fordrings on the beach, and how after the trial he hid it where no one would look. Beneath the paint of a picture of the twin moons, deep in what is now the Scarlet Bastion of Stratholme, lay his masterwork, Of Love and Family. At the sight of it Tirion nearly collapsed, sobbing.

He fell to one knee, and for a moment it seemed the fury of ages would be loosed upon the town. For years, he confessed, he had been the Grand Crusader's puppet, kept alive only by memories of his father and by dreams of fighting at his side. He wanted to dream no more. He asked to be taken to Tirion, and led the way out through Hearthglen toward the forest's edge.

title: The Annals of Darrowshire
body: Two threads of Darrowshire's story lead here. In the ruined inn of Andorhal, the bronze dragon Chromie believes the fate of Joseph Redpath, a doomed hero of that battle, can still be changed, but first it must be learned, and she sends for the Annals of Darrowshire, a book held in Andorhal's city hall. At Light's Hope Chapel a man of the Argent Dawn dreams of Darrowshire's fallen defenders crying out to him. Many of them roam again as the Scourge's ghouls in Plaguewood and Corin's Crossing, and he asks that they be found and their souls set free.

title: The Battle of Darrowshire
body: With the relics of Darrowshire gathered, Davil Lightfire's libram, Joseph Redpath's cracked shield, the skull of Horgus and the shattered sword of Marduk, Chromie says they are reagents for a great spell, and one more is needed: skulls of the Scourge champions who fought at Darrowshire. Carlin Redpath hands over an enchanted crystal that resonates when passed over such a skull, and sends hunters to the Noxious Glade to the north and the Fungal Vale to the west. Chromie has told him that the spell will give them a chance to save Darrowshire.

title: The Blightcaller's Imbeciles
body: Sylvanas sends her promising soldiers east to Nathanos Blightcaller, one of the first of her champions, and he greets each as fodder for his hounds. Training at the Marris Stead is whatever he needs done. Recruits fetch living rot from the Scourge of Corin's Crossing and grind it down to feed the blighthounds, clear the plaguebats from his fields, raid Quel'Lithien Lodge for a registry of his mortal life that they are forbidden to read, and hunt Duskwing, an albino demon bat, and Borelgore, a maggot beast that has cost him whole regiments. He calls every one of them imbecile.

parts.body: The last task is his own. In life Nathanos was cut down on this very farm by a monstrous abomination and woke as Scourge, his mind bound to the Lich King's until Sylvanas freed him. He hunted the beast across the wastes for months until it fled into Stratholme, and now he wants it destroyed: the abomination Ramstein.

title: The Scarlet Oracle
body: The Undercity has resolved to strike back at the Scarlet Crusade. Sylvanas herself has asked Nathanos Blightcaller to send his most capable agents for a sensitive operation, though by his account his best were killed years ago and he must make do with what he has. The Grand Crusader sits safely in the Scarlet Bastion while his forces pour into Forsaken lands, desecrating their monuments and murdering their people. His command is too well defended to strike directly, but Forsaken deathstalkers have found a weakness: each day a report travels from the Crusade's central command to Tyr's Hand in the hands of the Crimson Courier.

title: The Light of Dawn
body: To the defenders of Light's Hope Chapel, it began as the end of the world. Highlord Darion Mograine marched the Lich King's army and the death knights of Acherus against the chapel, and Korfax, Lord Maxwell Tyrosus, Leonid Barthalomew, Duke Zverenhoff and the Dawn's defenders held as long as they could. Darion's own blade, the corrupted Ashbringer, had begun to defy him, and more than a hundred defenders had fallen when Tirion Fordring arrived. Tirion told Darion that his master knew what lay beneath the chapel and had sent him there to die.

Darion turned on his master and threw the Ashbringer to Tirion, in whose hands it was cleansed. Struck by the blade, the Lich King withdrew, swearing their next meeting would not be on holy ground.
